# Unify WebApp primary, alias, route, and offline serving contracts

Parent #2563. Problem: primary hosts, aliases, route canonicalization, and
offline/detach can disagree. Scope: one serving contract; fail closed on exact
tenancy/upstream ambiguity; report/refuse conflicting `/api` and `/api/` legacy
routes; detach only framework-owned `site`/`site_api` kinds; preserve unrelated
routes; require fresh authorization and tenant scope; provide restore path and
visible errors.

Plan: regress primary/alias parity, canonical routes, ambiguity refusal, scoped
detach, and restore; consolidate behavior without product redesign; run edge
tests (full tier if model/migration/shared-helper scope emerges);
release/install; verify primary, alias, offline, restore, HTTPS, Admin and AWS.

Live acceptance expanded the implementation contract: taking a WebApp offline
and restoring its primary address must retain every non-managed custom route.
Custom routes therefore become durable WebApp desired state, while per-vhost
route rows remain the materialized edge configuration. The migration must
backfill existing primary-vhost routes without copying framework-managed auth
paths. Verification tier is full because this changes the schema and shared
serving lifecycle.
